rules.title: Every decision record carries a Status; superseded ones link forward
rules.lesson: CTX-5 no LOCKED artifact without a forward supersede-link
rules.rationale: A frozen decision the repo has overtaken, with no in-file 'Superseded by', actively misdirects a reader.
rules.fix: Give each ADR a Status: field; when a decision reverses, flip the old one to Superseded and add 'Superseded by <id>' in the same commit.

rules.title: Sources of truth are declared
rules.rationale: Load-bearing values copied into N docs drift to M values; declaring owners is step one.
rules.fix: Populate config.sources_of_truth (e.g. status, facts, decisions) so each fact class has one home.

rules.title: No broken internal doc links
rules.lesson: CTX doc-drift: a dead link is provable drift
rules.rationale: A relative link to a doc/file that no longer exists is the most common, most mechanical form of doc rot — and it is deterministically checkable.
rules.fix: Fix or remove the broken links the check reports; wire the check into CI so new ones can't land.

rules.title: Long-lived docs carry a freshness contract
rules.lesson: CTX-6 freshness as a computed state
rules.rationale: A doc with no 'last reviewed' date can rot invisibly; a per-doc TTL turns silent staleness into a red check.
rules.fix: Add 'last_review_date' (or ttl_days) to the frontmatter of docs under config.freshness_globs; refresh on review. Opt-in: empty freshness_globs skips this rule.

rules.title: Every declared decision edge resolves to a file that exists
rules.lesson: CTX-5 a declared decision edge must resolve — whatever the verb
rules.rationale: CTX-02 checks a superseded ADR HAS a forward link; this checks that every edge a record declares — Supersedes, Superseded-by, Amends, Amended-by — actually resolves to a present decision file. A reader who follows 'Amends: ADR-0019' to nothing concludes the corpus is incomplete, not that the pointer is wrong.
rules.fix: Make each named target exist, or drop the declaration. Both directions of both relations count; a list may wrap onto the next line and text in parentheses is commentary, never a target ('Amends: ADR-0019 (D5 sizing)' declares one edge, to 0019).

rules.title: Generated files carry a 'DO NOT EDIT' provenance marker
rules.rationale: A generated file with no marker gets hand-edited and silently diverges from its source; the marker makes provenance machine-visible.
rules.fix: Prepend a 'Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.' header to generated files; list their globs in config.generated_globs. Opt-in: empty generated_globs skips this rule.

check.pattern: Code generated .*DO NOT EDIT|@generated|DO NOT EDIT

rules.title: Required grounding docs exist and are non-empty
rules.lesson: CTX-4 grounding docs have one home
rules.rationale: The architecture/tech-stack docs a new session relies on are only load-bearing if they exist and are non-empty at their declared home.
rules.fix: List the grounding docs you rely on in config.grounding_docs; create any that are missing/empty. Opt-in: empty grounding_docs skips this rule.

rules.title: Code symbols/paths named in docs still resolve
rules.rationale: A doc that cites a file path in backticks which no longer exists is silent drift; path-integrity catches the mechanical half.
rules.fix: Fix or update the backticked file paths the check reports as missing.

rules.title: Docs don't lag the code they anchor
rules.lesson: docs trailing code is the drift the lessons are about
rules.rationale: A doc that declares which source files it documents is stale if that code was committed well after the doc; git dates make this checkable. Opt-in: only docs with a frontmatter 'sources:' list are checked.
rules.fix: Add 'sources: [glob, ...]' to the frontmatter of docs that track specific code; refresh the doc when that code changes (tune config.doc_lag_days).

rules.title: No hand-maintained status stamp (derive it instead)
rules.source: V2 ADR-0009 — a stored status stamp manufactures the multi-lane collision class it exists to prevent; state is derived by `baseline orient`, not hand-stamped
rules.lesson: CTX-12 stored-status signature — the V1 stamp artifact (retired at M7) is a blocker wherever it appears
rules.rationale: A hand-maintained freshness stamp is a stored proxy for derived state: it drifts, it collides under concurrent lanes, and it misdirects the next session (the ADR-0009 artifact). The stored-status surface retired at M7 — the deterministic line-anchored signature is the whole check, keyed to no config. MIGRATION.md walks the exit.
rules.fix: Delete the stamp line and run `baseline orient` for derived state; the stamp's job moves to the tree/history/forge derivation (see MIGRATION.md).

rules.title: An amendment is declared at both ends
rules.lesson: CTX-5 the amended record is the one a citation arrives at — it must know it was corrected
rules.rationale: Supersession is terminal: the reader is sent elsewhere and the dead end is loud. Amendment is what a decision does when part of it survives, so the amended record stays reachable and stays cited — and a one-way 'Amends:' leaves it silently standing on a premise a later record withdrew. Measured on a 36-ADR corpus: 18 amendment edges to 4 supersede-shaped ones, and 15 of the 18 declared in one direction only, none of them found by a check.
rules.fix: In the same commit as the amendment, write both ends: 'Amends: ADR-000X (what it changes)' on the new record and 'Amended-by: ADR-00YY' on the amended one. A corpus with history that cannot back-fill today records a judgment instead — `baseline jdg new --kind deviation --subject "docs/decisions/00XX-*.md" --reason "…" --review-by <date>` — and deleting it is how the repair is proved. The subject is a GLOB, so a corpus-wide subject sanctions future one-way edges too; scope it to the records you mean.

rules.title: No two decision records claim the same number
rules.lesson: CTX-5 the decision-record number IS the record's identity — a citation that resolves to two files resolves to neither
rules.rationale: Every consumer of the corpus — CTX-07's edge resolution, CTX-13's amendment pairing, a human following 'see ADR-0027' — reads the number off the filename and expects one record back. Two lanes authored an 0027 under different filenames: each tree was clean, neither merge conflicted, and the default branch ended with two ADR-0027s that no check had an opinion about. This is the floor that stops the collision SURVIVING (the branch that merges second turns the gate red). A gap in the sequence is reported in the detail and is deliberately not a finding.
rules.fix: Renumber one record to the next free number and update the edges pointing at it. If the corpus cannot renumber without breaking citations, record a judgment naming either colliding file — `baseline jdg new --kind deviation --subject "docs/decisions/00XX-*.md" --reason "…" --review-by <date>` — and deleting it is how the repair is proved. Reserve the number on the branch, before the merge, so the collision never lands.
